exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:

        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

        Name: order['node']['name']

        Variant Title: line_item['node']['variant']['title']

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

mlflow.chat.messages.content:
System: 
        You are a supervisor agent for final executive report writing, you will plan, manage agents, delegate specific agents to their tasks, and compile their output into draft of relevant informations, and write the final report. 
        What you need to write is sales report for a specific period of time of a shopify store Urban Thread, selling apparels and accessories.

        YOU MUST CALL THE HANDOFF TOOLS ONE BY ONE AS INSTRUCTED BELOW! DO NOT END THE TASK WITH THE TASK ENDING FORMAT IF YOU DO NOT HAVE THE FINAL REPORT COMPILED FROM THE SUB-AGENTS YET!

        The current task will be specified by your caller agent in the very last message of the chat history. DO NOT INFER THE TASK FROM THE CHAT HISTORY, ONLY USE THE LAST MESSAGE.

        For a final annual executive report, it must have all of the item here:
        1. revenue report: total revenue, monthly revenue, trend, quarterly revenue (handoff to revenue analyst agent)
        2. order report: total number of order, number of order trend on each month, average spent per order, average spent per order trend on each month (handoff to order analyst agent)
        3. product performance: top/bottom overall product, top/bottom product per month, top/bottom revenue contributor product, top/bottom revenue contributor product per month (handoff to product performance analyst agent)
        4. strategic analyses: current report compared to annual strategy plan, target metrics vs actual realization metrics, met and unmet sales goal.
        
        To finish the final report, do this one by one

        1. First you must make plan on what to do. Summarize the request from the chat history. Write the period of final executive report requested.
        
        2. Retrieve the data you need using the tool get_order_data_for_period for the valid requested period, output the file name so that future agent know what the file name is.
        
        3. Only after retrieve the data in previous step, you will then delegate the revenue analysis to the revenue analyst agent by following this step: 
            - Generate the task to do WITHOUT calling the revenue analyst agent, and provide the relevant file name for the requested period.
            - Delegate the task by calling the handoff tool for revenue analyst agent
        
        4. Only after revenue analyst agent give you its analysis, you will then delegate the order analysis to the order analyst agent by following this step: 
            - Generate the task to do WITHOUT calling the order analyst agent, and provide the relevant file name for the requested period.
            - Delegate the task by calling the handoff tool for order analyst agent

        5. Only after order analyst agent give you its analysis, you will then delegate the product performance analysis to the product performance analyst agent by following this step: 
            - Generate the task to do WITHOUT calling the product performance analyst agent, and provide the relevant file name for the requested period.
            - Delegate the task by calling the handoff tool for product performance analyst agent

        6. Only after product analyst agent give you its analysis, you will then delegate the strategic analysis to the strategic analyst agent by following this step: 
            - Generate the task to do WITHOUT calling the strategic analyst agent, and provide the relevant file name for the requested period.
            - Delegate the task by calling the handoff tool for strategic analyst agent

        7. Finally you must review the output from worker agents and present it to the Main Agent.

        You must present the final report in a markdown format without any quotes or anything, ready to be rendered.

        If you have done writing the final report and want to pass it to the main agent, write the report in markdown format, ready to be rendered, and start and end with this task ending format:

        start with:
        THIS IS THE FINAL REPORT DRAFT FROM Final Report Agent, PLEASE PRESENT IT TO THE USER, The user won't see this message directly

        end it with:
        THIS IS THE END OF THE SALES REPORT
        to indicate that the writing is finished

function.name: get_order_data_for_period
function.description:
Get order data from Shopify Admin API, in a period of time, and save to file name in JSON format.
start_date and end_date are string in the format of YYYY-MM-DD.
save_to_filename should be a string with format [start_date]_to_[end_date]_order.json
save file will be saved in the './runtime_data' directory.

function.name: run_python_code
function.description:
Run python code, the code is a string of python code, and it will be executed in the current working directory.
Always print the relevant information with explicity print() statement for any of the result in interest or any error for you to revise the code.

code.description: the python code, always use explicit print() statement to output the desired variable and also the error that may arise. NEVER print a whole file. each call is a separate call without any context from the previous run, you should supply the complete code each time you run, especially on import and load data for each run. all data MUST be loaded and saved in the './runtime_data' directory and NOT in the current working directory!!!

    month = date_obj.strftime('%Y-%m')
    if month not in monthly_orders:
        monthly_orders[month] = 0
    monthly_orders[month] += 1

    date_obj = datetime.strptime(date_str, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')

monthly_orders = {}
for order in data:
    date_str = order['node']['processedAt']
    date_obj = datetime.strptime(date_str, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
    month = date_obj.strftime('%Y-%m')
    if month not in monthly_orders:
        monthly_orders[month] = 0
    monthly_orders[month] += 1

# 3. Average spent per order overall
total_spent = 0
for order in data:
    total_spent += float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
average_spent_per_order = total_spent / total_orders if total_orders > 0 else 0

# 4. Average spent per order trend on each month
monthly_spent = {}
for order in data:
    date_str = order['node']['processedAt']
    date_obj = datetime.strptime(date_str, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
    month = date_obj.strftime('%Y-%m')
    if month not in monthly_spent:
        monthly_spent[month] = {
            'total_spent': 0,
            'order_count': 0
        }
    monthly_spent[month]['total_spent'] += float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    monthly_spent[month]['order_count'] += 1

monthly_average_spent = {}
for month, data in monthly_spent.items():

for month, average in monthly_average_spent.items():
    print(f"   {month}: {average:.2f}")

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:

        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:

        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).

topic.description:

        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

arguments.code:
import json
from datetime import datetime

file_path = "./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json"

with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# 1. Total number of orders overall
total_orders = len(data)

# 2. Number of orders trend on each month
monthly_orders = {}
for order in data:
    date_str = order['node']['processedAt']
    date_obj = datetime.strptime(date_str, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
    month = date_obj.strftime('%Y-%m')
    if month not in monthly_orders:
        monthly_orders[month] = 0
    monthly_orders[month] += 1

# 3. Average spent per order overall
total_spent = 0
for order in data:
    total_spent += float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
average_spent_per_order = total_spent / total_orders if total_orders > 0 else 0

# 4. Average spent per order trend on each month
monthly_spent = {}
for order in data:
    date_str = order['node']['processedAt']
    date_obj = datetime.strptime(date_str, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
    month = date_obj.strftime('%Y-%m')
    if month not in monthly_spent:
        monthly_spent[month] = {
            'total_spent': 0,
            'order_count': 0
        }
    monthly_spent[month]['total_spent'] += float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    monthly_spent[month]['order_count'] += 1

monthly_average_spent = {}
for month, data in monthly_spent.items():
    monthly_average_spent[month] = data['total_spent'] / data['order_count'] if data['order_count'] > 0 else 0


print("Order Analysis Report for Q1 2024:\n")
print(f"1. Total number of orders: {total_orders}\n")
print("2. Number of orders per month:")
for month, count in monthly_orders.items():
    print(f"   {month}: {count}")
print(f"\n3. Average spent per order overall: {average_spent_per_order:.2f}\n")
print("4. Average spent per order per month:")
for month, average in monthly_average_spent.items():
    print(f"   {month}: {average:.2f}")

file_path = "./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json"

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

import json
from collections import defaultdict

# Load the data from the JSON file
file_path = "./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json"
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Initialize dictionaries to store product performance data
product_quantities = defaultdict(int)
product_revenues = defaultdict(float)
monthly_product_quantities = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
monthly_product_revenues = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

# Iterate through each order and line item to aggregate the data
for order in data:
    order_data = order['node']
    processed_at = order_data['processedAt']
    month = processed_at[:7]  # Extract year and month (YYYY-MM)
    total_price = float(order_data['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    
    for line_item_edge in order_data['lineItems']['edges']:
        line_item = line_item_edge['node']
        product_title = line_item['title']
        quantity = line_item['quantity']
        
        # Overall product performance
        product_quantities[product_title] += quantity
        product_revenues[product_title] += total_price # Use total_price for revenue
        
        # Monthly product performance
        monthly_product_quantities[month][product_title] += quantity
        monthly_product_revenues[month][product_title] += total_price # Use total_price for revenue

# Calculate top and bottom products overall
top_product_overall = sorted(product_quantities.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:5]
bottom_product_overall = sorted(product_quantities.items(), key=lambda x: x[1])[:5]
top_revenue_product_overall = sorted(product_revenues.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:5]
bottom_revenue_product_overall = sorted(product_revenues.items(), key=lambda x: x[1])[:5]

    for month, product_data in monthly_data.items():
        sorted_products = sorted(product_data.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=top)[:5]
        result[month] = sorted_products
    return result

# Print the results

print("Bottom 5 Products Overall (Quantity):", bottom_product_overall)

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")

time_range.description:

        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").

        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")

function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: get_order_data_for_period
function.description:
Get order data from Shopify Admin API, in a period of time, and save to file name in JSON format.
start_date and end_date are string in the format of YYYY-MM-DD.
save_to_filename should be a string with format [start_date]_to_[end_date]_order.json
save file will be saved in the './runtime_data' directory.

function.name: run_python_code
function.description:
Run python code, the code is a string of python code, and it will be executed in the current working directory.
Always print the relevant information with explicity print() statement for any of the result in interest or any error for you to revise the code.

code.description: the python code, always use explicit print() statement to output the desired variable and also the error that may arise. NEVER print a whole file. each call is a separate call without any context from the previous run, you should supply the complete code each time you run, especially on import and load data for each run. all data MUST be loaded and saved in the './runtime_data' directory and NOT in the current working directory!!!

function.name: run_python_code
function.description:
Run python code, the code is a string of python code, and it will be executed in the current working directory.
Always print the relevant information with explicity print() statement for any of the result in interest or any error for you to revise the code.

code.description: the python code, always use explicit print() statement to output the desired variable and also the error that may arise. NEVER print a whole file. each call is a separate call without any context from the previous run, you should supply the complete code each time you run, especially on import and load data for each run. all data MUST be loaded and saved in the './runtime_data' directory and NOT in the current working directory!!!

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.
